blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Implements 32 32-bit integer registers with two asynchronous read ports, one rising-edge write port, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired x0 reads and writes.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps register state and x0 behavior isolated for straightforward verification; asynchronous reads support single-cycle execution.

blocks.name: immediate_generator
blocks.responsibility: Generates sign-extended I, S, B, and J immediates and the zero-extended U immediate from an instruction.
blocks.design_rationale: Centralizes immediate bit mapping, reducing duplicated logic and making instruction-format behavior easy to verify.

blocks.name: control_unit
blocks.responsibility: Decodes the instruction into register-write, memory-write, memory-width, operand-selection, ALU-operation, writeback-selection, immediate-selection, branch, and jump controls.
blocks.design_rationale: Separates instruction decoding from datapath calculations, making RV32I and RV32M control decisions independently verifiable.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Executes RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and comparisons, plus RV32M multiplication, division, and remainder operations; provides equality and signed and unsigned less-than flags for branches.
blocks.design_rationale: Groups the combinational execution datapath for a single-cycle design and allows arithmetic, comparison, and M-extension behavior to be tested as one block.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Top-level single-cycle RV32IM CPU. Instantiates the register file, immediate generator, control unit, and ALU; maintains the PC; performs branch and jump target selection, load extraction and extension, and store/load bus control; and exposes the instruction and data bus contract.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps PC sequencing and bus behavior at the contract boundary while composing independently verifiable datapath blocks into the required monociclo CPU.

notes: The ALU operation selector is an internal encoding shared by control_unit and alu. The CPU selects branch conditions using the decoded branch funct3 and ALU comparison flags; jump and branch targets use the generated immediates. Memory addresses remain byte addresses, and the CPU handles little-endian load selection and sign or zero extension.
